Let \(T\) be the top vertex, and let \(B\) and \(C\) be the left and right vertices. Let \(M\) and \(N\) be the black midpoint points on \(AB\) and \(AC\), respectively.

The shaded plane is \(\triangle TMN\), so the portion containing \(A\) is tetrahedron \(Tamn\).

Since \(M\) and \(N\) are midpoints,
\[
AM=\frac12 AB,\qquad AN=\frac12 AC.
\]
Thus \(\triangle AMN\sim\triangle ABC\) with scale factor \(1/2\), so
\[
\frac{[AMN]}{[ABC]}=\left(\frac12\right)^2=\frac14.
\]

Tetrahedra \(Tamn\) and \(TABC\) have the same altitude from \(T\) to the plane \(ABC\). Therefore their volumes have the same ratio as their bases:
\[
\frac{V_{Tamn}}{V_{TABC}}=\frac14.
\]

Hence
\[
V_{Tamn}=\frac14(120)=\boxed{30}.
\]
